correctness.rationale: For the exact iid erased-or-one-step-stale iteration, the 2-by-2 covariance operator is primitive at third power. Its Perron eigenvalue therefore is the asymptotic squared-error factor for every nonzero deterministic initial state. Direct determinant and resultant identities give the characteristic cubic and optimizer cubic. F(1,h), a strict lower bound on Perron r, positivity of F_r, and strict concavity of Q on [0,h_c] imply exact stability and unique global minimization. Q_p<0 and Q_h<0 on the larger-root branch prove h_* strictly decreasing. Exact series and a positive Perron functional prove the endpoint laws and strict gap to fresh packets. The standalone verifier reproduces key identities, 405 exact-rational finite branch/moment checks and 99 supplemental numerical optimizer comparisons; numerical tests do not substitute for the proof. Boundaries are 0<p<1 and h>0.

originality.rationale: The acceptance claim is the unique reliability-dependent global mean-square rate optimizer, its exact cubic and strictly decreasing optimal-gain law for erased one-step-stale gradient packets. value.rationale: For a natural optimization feedback constraint—independently erased one-step-old gradients—the globally best fixed learning rate is not the stability ceiling or the delay-free optimizer. The cubic gives exact usable calibration at every delivery probability, proves monotone movement between limiting gains 1 and 1/4, and quantifies the irreducible second-moment rate cost of staleness. It is a motivated scalar baseline for intermittent delayed-gradient methods rather than arbitrary parameter numerology. Finite-horizon and multidimensional extensions are unproved.
